title: Largest Merged Code
body:
You have two lists of digits. Build the largest possible number of exactly k digits by choosing digits from both lists. Digits taken from the same list must keep their original relative order, but you can interleave the two lists however you like.

Print the digits of the largest number.

Function to complete

Complete largestMerged(a, b, k). It returns the k digits of the largest code.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: m. Line 2: m digits. Line 3: n. Line 4: n digits. Line 5: k.

samples.ex: Take [7] from the first list and [8, 2, 5, 6] from the second. Merged: 8 7 2 5 6.
[6, 5] from the first list and [9, 8, 3] from the second.

py.pre:
from typing import *
import sys, math, collections, heapq, bisect, itertools, functools
from collections import *
py.post:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _m = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    a = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_m)])); _p += (_m)
    _n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    b = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_n)])); _p += (_n)
    k = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _r = Solution().largestMerged(a, b, k)
    print(" ".join(map(str, _r)))
